numbering.explanation: Engineer digits 1–9 choose a top-level heading and Yes enters it. Submenu digits have meaning only within that heading. Zone addresses are three digits; configuration numbers, output type values, attribute positions and user-type values are separate namespaces. Record fields are often advanced with Yes, not addressed by digits.

examples.meaning: Engineer Utils → View Zone Status. Then 002 selects zone 002; 002 is a zone address.
In the existing training route, select zone 003 then change its type to Guard. The last 3 is a type value.
Global Options → System Config. → configuration 07, Remove Omits / Leave Omits. 07 is the configuration-item number.
Omit Zones in INS177-9 p14. INS176-9 p46 prints a different assignment; do not interchange them.

caveats: FINDR’s order field is source/presentation order, not a shortcut.
The schema code field contains a local documented identifier; selection/reference values are not executable full routes.
Names such as Guard and Omit Zones are manufacturer wording; everyday aliases are FINDR search aids.
Three digits select a zone; 24/48/88/168/640 are panel capacities/model names, not menu numbers.
Do not combine older installer numbering with newer quick-guide additions without a firmware match.

navigation.action: At a numbered menu, choose a documented option and enter it. The numeric context changes inside records and value editors.
Browse options/records. In the log, down goes backward in time and up moves forward.
Yes enters or accepts. No edits/toggles in the relevant field. In Zone Setup, Yes steps through fields and scroll changes the selected zone.
Distinct controls with context-specific return and exit behaviour. A programming exit can leave the engineer logged on; 0 Log off ENGINEER then Yes ends that session.
At the authorised user prompt, opens ordinary omission; within its list toggles the selected zone. In Engineer View Zone Status it instead invokes a diagnostic disable cleared on leaving.
Contextual keys: area selection or alternate displays, test/chime functions, and part-arm/log-text functions. They are not globally interchangeable navigation keys.
